generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential from 1; never NULL; unique per table; never targeted by duplicate planting or group-size planting.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the final parent PK pool (after all parent dedupe and NULL planting); 5-30% NULL only where the column is nullable; otherwise always a valid parent key. Re-validate FK after all planting.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random word-like token 3-20 chars; 5% near-variant (case flip, trailing space, doubled char) of a pool literal.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random capitalized given/surname from a 40-name pool; 5% near-variant (lowercase, typo) of a pool literal.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Number + street word + suffix; city/state/country from small pools.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_phone: Random digits with optional +, -, (), x separators, 10-15 chars.
generic_sampling_rules.double_amount: Uniform 0..10000 with 2 decimals; 5-30% NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_short: Pick uniformly from the column's enum list.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, include L, L-step, L+step where step is 1 for integers and 0.01 for doubles.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_text: For each listed literal L, include L and a case-variant (lower/upper) and a one-char typo.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_date: For each listed literal L, include L, L-1 day, L+1 day in the column format.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: Ensure 20-50% of non-NULL values repeat an earlier value in the same column; never applied to primary-key columns.
generic_sampling_rules.ties_for_order_limit: Ensure at least 3 rows share the same value at the listed ORDER rank.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, 5-30% of rows NULL; at least one NULL per nullable column per instance; never applied to PK columns; applied exactly once per column (FK NULL path or generic path, not both).
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: Ensure groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 exist on the grouped column; applied to the final column values after all planting; never applied to a primary-key column.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: For each join column, ensure at least one parent row has no child and at least one child FK points to a valid parent (no orphan unless nullable). For NOT NULL child FKs, achieve parent-childlessness by redirecting/removing child rows, never by setting the FK to NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary: For each listed aggregate target, plant child-row counts so that COUNT(*) and COUNT(col) take the values 1, 2 and >=3 across parent groups; NULLs in the counted column reduce COUNT(col) but not COUNT(*); use the instance rng for parent selection; preserve planted NULLs in the counted column.

date_left_staff IS NULL OR date_joined_staff IS NULL OR date_left_staff >= date_joined_staff

The compact DB already has 3 Vehicles rows, so the final Vehicles table has 3 compact + 6 generated = 9 rows; the 6 generated rows are needed to make group_sizes (1,2,>=3) on vehicle_details achievable.
No formula relates amount_outstanding to payments or lesson price; none is stated.
lesson_time is a free-form VARCHAR(10); boundary values '' and 'x' are targeted and the column is also nullable, so boundary literals appear among non-NULL rows and NULLs are planted separately.

Customer_Payments composite PK (customer_id, datetime_payment) is enforced by generation order and unique datetime per customer; datetime_payment is sampled per customer with uniqueness; composite PK dedupe must not drop rows needed for aggregate-boundary planting.
Staff.date_of_birth values in the sample include minors (2010-2015); no age constraint is asserted, and no minimum-age is intended.
No FK enforcement is enabled in the writer; FK targets are sampled from the final parent PK pool after all dedupe and NULL planting, and a post-generation FK validation is required.
Duplicate planting is applied to primary-key columns only where the final PK is not required to be unique; the program should dedupe PKs after planting and re-validate FK references.
The instance file is the compact database plus appended generated rows; the original DB path must be passed through to the writer so compact rows are copied.

Aggregate-boundary targets (COUNT(*) > 2 with counts 1,2,>=3) must be planted explicitly for Customers.customer_id and Customer_Payments.customer_id/amount_payment; the parent-side group sizes (Customers.customer_id) must take 1, 2 and >=3 across the full parent set, not just 3 parents with 1/2/3 and the rest 0.

Customers.customer_id group_sizes is achieved via the child-side (Customer_Payments.customer_id) distribution, not by planting duplicates on the PK column; _plant_group_sizes must never be applied to a primary-key column.

Nullable FK NULL share must be computed once from _null_share(rng) and applied as a single target count; the previous double mechanism (0.15 pre-threshold plus _plant_nulls) could exceed the 5-30% cap. Lessons.staff_id is handled solely by the FK NULL path and must be removed from NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS.
Each nullable column must receive at least one NULL per instance; a post-generation assertion should verify this across all instances.
The lesson_date >= '2015-01-01' rule is removed from semantic_rules_and_formulas; the DateSampler range (2015-01-01..2018-03-31) already satisfies it by construction.

The writer should enable foreign_keys=ON before any transaction (or run PRAGMA foreign_key_check after commit) and raise on violations; generated parent PKs must be a superset of the original PKs so compact child rows still resolve.
The writer should open the compact DB read-only and use the sqlite3 backup API or VACUUM INTO to create a consistent copy, or ensure the original is not in WAL mode.

max_l0 in the sampler must be at least 3 for columns in GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS and large enough for 20-50% duplicates on DUPLICATE_COLUMNS, so that group_sizes and duplicates_for_distinct targets remain achievable.

After fixing aggregate-boundary and group-size planting, re-run the construction check and verify that construction_pairs_by_group is populated and separated count increases; add a post-generation assertion that for each AGGREGATE_BOUNDARY triple, the child-row counts per parent include 1, 2 and >=3, and that COUNT(counted_col) also includes 1, 2 and >=3.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: integrity.fk_violations = 749 across 20 instances, and validity.reasons.new_integrity_failures = 20 (every instance). The writer (writer.py) sets `pragma foreign_keys = OFF` and inserts generated rows without validating FK targets; instance.py draws FKs from `key_pool[pt]`, but the pool is extended with generated keys only *after* the child table is built in `order`, and `_compact_keys`/`_next_int_key` can produce keys that are later dropped by `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` (e.g. composite PK Customer_Payments, or dedupe of Vehicles.vehicle_id), leaving child FKs pointing at keys that never get inserted. The spec's `unmatched_join_rows` rule explicitly requires 'no orphan unless nullable', which is violated.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK generation reference only keys that actually survive into the parent table: build parent tables fully (including PK dedupe) before sampling child FKs, or re-validate/repair child FKs against the final parent key set. Enable `pragma foreign_keys = ON` (or run a post-insert FK check) so violations are caught, and ensure the `unmatched_join_rows` rule (parent without children + no orphan) holds. Re-run and confirm fk_violations = 0.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.reasons.compact_rows_missing = 20 (all instances). writer.py's `write_instance_sqlite` is called from cli.py as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with no `orig_path`, so the `if orig_path and os.path.exists(orig_path)` branch is skipped and the file is created fresh from `schema.ddl` — the compact rows are never copied. The module docstring and spec both state instances are 'copies of the compact database plus appended generated rows'.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original DB path through to `write_instance_sqlite` (e.g. store `orig` in `_G['args']` and forward it), so the instance file is a copy of the compact DB before appending. Verify compact_rows_missing = 0 after the fix.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: nullable_columns shows 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' for many nullable columns that the spec lists in `null_targets` (e.g. Addresses.city/country/zip/state/line_1, Customers.first_name/last_name/email/phone/cell/date_of_birth/date_became_customer, Staff.first_name/last_name/middle_name/nickname/date_of_birth/date_joined/date_left, Lessons.lesson_date/lesson_time/price, Vehicles.vehicle_details, Customer_Payments.amount_payment). spec.NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS only contains two entries (Customers.amount_outstanding, Lessons.staff_id), so the program does not plant NULLs for the other nullable columns despite the interface rule requiring at least one NULL per nullable column per instance.
issues.requested_revision: Extend NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS (or derive it from the schema's nullable columns) to cover every nullable column in `null_targets`, and plant NULLs per the compact share (5-30%, at least one). Note: per instruction 7 this is a non-blocking observation, but it should be fixed for spec fidelity.

issues.evidence: Spec `per_column_exceptions` lists `Customers.customer_status_code` enum targets including 'good customer' (lowercase), and `ENUMS` in spec.py includes it, but the semantic formula `_f_customer_status` only accepts ('Good Customer','Bad Customer'). `_apply_formula` repairs any 'good customer' value to one of the two canonical values, so the lowercase enum variant can never survive — the enum target and the formula are mutually inconsistent.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the enum list with the formula: either drop 'good customer' from the enum targets, or relax the formula to accept the case-variant (and document the intended semantics).

issues.evidence: Spec `per_column_exceptions` includes `Lessons.lesson_time` comparison_boundary targets ['', 'x'], and `BOUNDARY_TEXT` encodes them, but `Lessons.lesson_time` is also in `null_targets` and the interface rule requires NULLs there; the boundary sampler (BoundaryTextSampler) never emits NULL, and `_plant_nulls` is only applied for columns in NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS (lesson_time is not). The two rules are not jointly satisfiable as written.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify precedence: either add lesson_time to NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS and ensure boundary literals still appear among non-NULL rows, or remove it from null_targets. Document the intended interaction.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_plant_group_sizes` and `_plant_duplicates` operate on the *generated* column values only, but `GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS` includes ('Customer_Payments','customer_id') and ('Vehicles','vehicle_details'), and `DUPLICATE_COLUMNS` includes ('Vehicles','vehicle_id') and ('Lessons','lesson_id') which are primary keys. For PK columns, `_next_int_key` assigns fresh sequential keys, then `_plant_duplicates` overwrites some with earlier values, and `sample_fresh_primary_keys` then drops the duplicates — so the duplicate share is not actually achieved on PK columns, and the group-size rule on customer_id (a FK) is applied before FK re-sampling may overwrite it. The construction_pairs feedback (separated 27/155) is consistent with these rules not being reliably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Apply duplicate/group-size planting to the final column values (after PK dedupe and FK assignment), and do not target primary-key columns for duplicates_for_distinct (or handle the dedupe interaction explicitly). Verify group sizes 1/2/>=3 and 20-50% duplicate share on the final data.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_formula` repairs values using only the single column's value (`row = {col: v}`), so cross-column formulas like `_f_date_became` (needs date_of_birth), `_f_date_left`/`_f_date_joined` (need the other date) always see the other operand as None and pass trivially; the actual enforcement relies on `_fix_date_order`, which only runs for Staff and Customers and only fixes `later < earlier` by pushing `later` forward — it does not handle the case where `date_of_birth` is NULL but `date_became_customer` is set, nor does it re-check after `_plant_duplicates`/`_plant_different_values` may have altered dates. The `date_became_customer` rows_with_different_values planting (`_plant_different_values`) can set a value that violates `>= date_of_birth`.
issues.requested_revision: Enforce cross-column date formulas on the final row values (after all planting), and re-run `_fix_date_order` last. Ensure `_plant_different_values` respects the date_became_customer >= date_of_birth constraint.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_plant_nulls` is applied to `Lessons.staff_id` (nullable FK) and `Customers.amount_outstanding`, but the FK sampling for `Lessons.staff_id` happens before `_plant_nulls` and the NULL planting uses `_null_share` from the compact DB; however `_plant_nulls` can also NULL out a value that was the only non-NULL in a group, and the `unmatched_join_rows` rule for `Lessons.vehicle_id` (in UNMATCHED_JOIN) is not actually enforced anywhere — there is no code that guarantees a parent row without children or a child pointing to a parent. The `UNMATCHED_JOIN` list is declared but never consulted in instance.py.
issues.requested_revision: Implement the unmatched_join_rows rule: after building all tables, ensure at least one parent row (Addresses, Customers, Staff) has no referencing child, and at least one child FK points to a valid parent. Remove or wire up the unused UNMATCHED_JOIN list.

issues.evidence: Spec `uncertainty` notes 'Staff.date_of_birth values in the sample include minors (2010-2015); no age constraint is asserted', and the supporting_evidence shows Staff row 1 dob 2010-12-08 joined 2017-04-27. issues.evidence: instance.py _build_table FK assignment uses float threshold rng.random() > 0.15 to introduce NULLs on nullable FKs, and then calls _plant_nulls(vals, rng, share) on the SAME list. _plant_nulls unconditionally overwrites a random sample of positions with NULL (k = round(n*share)), so for non-nullable FK columns whose FK is set to a valid parent, no NULL is planted (correct), but for nullable FK, two independent NULL mechanisms combine. The 0.15 pre-threshold already lets roughly 15% NULL, and _plant_nulls on top yields ~5-30% more, which can violate the spec's '5-30% NULL' share cap. The secondary validation is not enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Compute a single target NULL count from _null_share(rng), then sample that many distinct FK rows to be NULL, otherwise always set the FK to a valid parent key. Validate final NULL share against [0.05, 0.30] after all planting.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_nulls silently skips planting for empty values. Instance sizes are large enough (>=9) that this is fine, but if a column values list has length n=1 (possible on small tables like Vehicles size 3 with duplicates already restricting) at least one NULL is required per nullable column per instance per the NULL rule. The spec requires 'at least one NULL per nullable column per instance', while the current piping cannot enforce that Vehicles.vehicle_details also receives NULL and non-NULL rows in every instance. Execution feedback only reports NULLs for Vehicles.vehicle_details 1/4 across 20 instances - far below one NULL per nullable column per instance. Many of the 20 instances likely have zero NULLs in Vehicles.vehicle_details.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee exactly one NULL per nullable column per instance: after all planting, if a nullable column has zero NULLs, force-replace one row's value with NULL (unless doing so would break a semantic formula or PK). Conversely ensure at least one non-NULL value remains. Add a post-generation assertion that verifies this across all 20 instances.

issues.evidence: Supported semantic rules from supporting_evidence: customer_status_code enum (rows 1-2), payment_method_code enum (rows 1-2), lesson_status_code enum (rows 1-2), vehicle_details enum (rows 1-3), date_left_staff >= date_joined_staff (3 example rows), date_joined_staff >= date_of_birth (3 example rows, but Staff row 1 dob is 2010-12-08, i.e., a 7-year-old employee - weak evidence, but the spec note 'no age constraint is intended' is acknowledged), date_became_customer >= date_of_birth (3 example rows), amounts >= 0. issues.evidence: writer.py copies the original DB (orig_path) into the part file before inserting ALL generated rows (sizes vary 9-21 per table). Rows are concatenated, not preserved-discriminated. Compact rows are never modified (good), but the FK check is only done in SQLite at write time (foreign_keys=OFF during insert, so no check). The automated integrity report says fk_violations=0 for 20 instances, but the SQLite check is disabled during write and the validator runs later. There is also no post-generation FK validation code path in the provided program (only re-validate FK per instance is mentioned in spec uncertainty, but no code enforces it).

Also assert that generated parent PKs (Vehicles.vehicle_id, Staff.staff_id, Customers.customer_id, Addresses.address_id) correspond to a superset of the original PKs, so existing compact child rows still resolve. issues.evidence: Construction feedback: construction_pairs separated=5 of 155 eligible. issues.evidence: spec.py AGGREGATE_BOUNDARY lists ('Customers','customer_id','Customer_Payments','customer_id','customer_id') and ('Customers','customer_id','Customer_Payments','customer_id','amount_payment'). instance.py _plant_aggregate_boundary assigns child rows to only 3 parents (1,2,3 rows) and leaves the remaining 12 Customers with 0 payments. issues.evidence: instance.py _ensure_unmatched sets a child FK to None when all parents are used, but for NOT NULL FK columns (e.g. Customers.customer_address_id, Lessons.vehicle_id, Lessons.customer_id, Customer_Payments.customer_id) this would violate NOT NULL. The writer's foreign_key_check would then raise. The construction feedback shows 0 FK violations for the 20 instances, but the logic is fragile: _ensure_unmatched is called for every (parent, child) pair in spec.UNMATCHED_JOIN, and for Customers.customer_id it iterates all child tables including Customer_Payments and Lessons; if all Customers are used, it nulls a Customer_Payments.customer_id (NOT NULL) or Lessons.customer_id (NOT NULL).
issues.requested_revision: In _ensure_unmatched, only null out a child FK if the column is nullable; otherwise, instead of nulling, remove/redirect a child row so a parent becomes childless without violating NOT NULL. Re-validate FK and NOT NULL after this step.

issues.evidence: instance.py _build_table: for composite PK Customer_Payments, pk_cols = ['customer_id','datetime_payment']. The code fills data['customer_id'] from FK assignment (nullable? customer_id is NOT NULL per schema), then 'if all(v is None for v in data[pc])' fills with range(1,n+1) — but customer_id is already populated from FK, so this branch is skipped. datetime_payment is sampled by random_values_for_a_column (DateSampler) and is not guaranteed unique per customer. The writer's PK dedupe drops duplicate (customer_id, datetime_payment) tuples, which can silently reduce Customer_Payments row count below 15 and break the aggregate-boundary planting (which assumes 6 child rows assigned to 3 parents).
issues.requested_revision: Explicitly generate datetime_payment unique per customer_id (e.g., sample distinct timestamps per customer group), and ensure the composite PK dedupe does not drop rows needed for aggregate-boundary planting. Add a post-generation assertion that Customer_Payments has the expected row count and that (customer_id, datetime_payment) is unique.

issues.evidence: spec.py NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS includes ('Lessons','staff_id') and ('Lessons','lesson_time'), and instance.py _build_table plants NULLs for nullable FK staff_id via the single _null_share mechanism, then later _plant_nulls is applied again for columns in NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS (including staff_id). issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_group_sizes requires n >= 6 and picks distinct[0], distinct[1], distinct[2]. For Vehicles.vehicle_details with TABLE_SIZES Vehicles=6 and enum ['Van','Truck','Car'], this works. But for Customers.customer_id (PK, sequential 1..15), _plant_group_sizes is applied to the PK column, overwriting PK values with duplicates of distinct[0..2]. For Customers.customer_id group_sizes, achieve 1,2,>=3 via the child-side (Customer_Payments.customer_id) distribution instead, or plant group sizes on a non-PK column. issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include Customers.customer_id group_sizes with targets ['1,2,>=3'] and the uncertainty note states 'Customers.customer_id group_sizes is achieved via the child-side (Customer_Payments.customer_id) distribution, not by planting duplicates on the PK column; _plant_group_sizes must never be applied to a primary-key column.' spec.GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS includes ('Customer_Payments','customer_id') and ('Vehicles','vehicle_details'), which is correct. However, _plant_group_sizes in instance.py is applied to Customer_Payments.customer_id, which is a FK column, not a PK column — that is fine. But the group_sizes target for Customer_Payments.customer_id requires groups of size 1, 2, and >=3, and _plant_group_sizes only sets 6 positions (order[0..5]) to a, b, b, c, c, c. With n=15 rows, this creates groups of size 1 (a), 2 (b), and 3 (c), but the remaining 9 rows keep their original values, which may create additional groups. This is acceptable for the target, but the aggregate_boundary planting in _plant_aggregate_boundary then overwrites child_fk values for the first 6 rows, potentially destroying the group_sizes planting. The order of operations in build_random_instance: _build_table (which includes _plant_group_sizes) runs first, then _plant_aggregate_boundary overwrites child_fk for the first 6 rows. This means the group_sizes planting on Customer_Payments.customer_id is overwritten by aggregate_boundary planting, so the group_sizes target may not be satisfied.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure that _plant_aggregate_boundary and _plant_group_sizes on Customer_Payments.customer_id are coordinated so both targets are satisfied. issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include Lessons.lesson_id duplicates_for_distinct with targets ['20-50%'] and Vehicles.vehicle_id duplicates_for_distinct with targets ['20-50%']. However, spec.DUPLICATE_COLUMNS does not include ('Lessons','lesson_id') or ('Vehicles','vehicle_id'). The specification's generic_sampling_rules state 'duplicates_for_distinct: Ensure 20-50% of non-NULL values repeat an earlier value in the same column; never applied to primary-key columns.' Since lesson_id and vehicle_id are primary keys, the generic rule says never apply duplicates to PK columns. But the per_column_exceptions explicitly list them as duplicates_for_distinct targets. This is a contradiction in the specification itself: the per_column_exceptions request duplicates on PK columns, while the generic rule forbids it. The program follows the generic rule (does not plant duplicates on PKs), which is the safer choice for integrity, but it does not implement the per_column_exceptions as written.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: resolve the contradiction between the generic rule ('never applied to primary-key columns') and the per_column_exceptions listing Lessons.lesson_id and Vehicles.vehicle_id as duplicates_for_distinct targets. Either remove these from per_column_exceptions or clarify that the generic rule takes precedence. Engineer: if the designer confirms PK duplicates are not intended, no code change is needed; otherwise, implement a mechanism that does not violate PK uniqueness (e.g., the duplicates_for_distinct pattern on a PK is likely a mis-extraction and should be dropped).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions list Customers.customer_id aggregate_boundary with targets ['COUNT(*) > 2', '1,2,>=3'] and Customers.customer_id group_sizes with targets ['1,2,>=3']. The uncertainty note says 'the parent-side group sizes (Customers.customer_id) must take 1, 2 and >=3 across the full parent set, not just 3 parents with 1/2/3 and the rest 0.' However, the specification's AGGREGATE_BOUNDARY in spec.py (engineer's implementation) only plants 1, 2, 3 for three parents and 0 for the rest. The designer's specification is ambiguous: it says 'plant child-row counts so that COUNT(*) and COUNT(col) take the values 1, 2 and >=3 across parent groups' but also says 'the parent-side group sizes (Customers.customer_id) must take 1, 2 and >=3 across the full parent set, not just 3 parents with 1/2/3 and the rest 0.' These two statements are contradictory: if only three parents have children (1, 2, 3) and the rest have 0, then the group sizes across the full parent set are 0, 0, ..., 1, 2, 3 — which does include 1, 2, and >=3, but the note says 'not just 3 parents with 1/2/3 and the rest 0.' The designer should clarify what 'across the full parent set' means.

If the intent is that all parents have at least one child (so group sizes are 1, 2, >=3 with no 0s), then the specification should say so explicitly.
